Synopsis:
    Australian equities dropped to a two-month low, dragged down by miners (BHP -4.1%, Rio Tinto -3.5%, lithium names -7-9%) on weaker commodity prices. A global risk-off mood prevailed, driven by oil above $100/bbl, persistent inflation, and Middle East supply disruption fears. RBA rate hike expectations firmed (32bps Nov, 39bps Dec), Australian bond yields crossed 5% for the first time since 2011. Copper slid on uncertainty around US refined copper tariffs. New Zealand equities also fell 1%.
